label: Three presentations of universal properties in Leinster’s textbook
summary: Leinster describes his introductory category theory textbook as presenting universal properties through adjoint functors, representable functors, and limits, with a final chapter tying the three approaches together.

label: Seven-sketch application tour of category theory
summary: Fong and Spivak describe seven instructional sketches pairing examples including databases, electric circuits, and dynamical systems with categorical structures including adjoint functors, enriched categories, and toposes.

sources.title: Seven Sketches in Compositionality: An Invitation to Applied Category Theory

label: Database schemas as categories and instances as functors
summary: Spivak proposes a database definition language in which a database schema is a small category and an instance is a set-valued functor on that schema.

label: Three schema-induced data-migration functors
summary: Within Spivak’s category-and-functor database model, morphisms of schemas induce three data-migration functors that translate instances between schemas in canonical ways.

label: Data-migration functors parameterize relational operations
summary: Spivak reports that the three data-migration functors parameterize projections, unions, and joins across all tables simultaneously in the categorical database formulation.

label: Categorical migration functors as alternatives to query types
summary: Spivak states that his three data-migration functors can be used in place of conjunctive and disjunctive queries within the paper’s database framework.

label: Functorial connection to functional-programming types
summary: Spivak describes connecting a database to a functional programming language by introducing a functorial connection between the database schema and the language’s category of types.

label: Higher Gray tensor generalization described as open
summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber describe the systematic construction of higher-dimensional analogues of the Gray tensor product as an open problem in higher category theory in their 2009-submitted paper.

sources.title: Algebras of higher operads as enriched categories II

label: Gray and Crans tensor products included in higher-operad theory
summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber state that their resulting theory includes the Gray tensor product of 2-categories and the Crans tensor product of Gray categories.

sources.title: Algebras of higher operads as enriched categories II

label: Reported Ekmann-Hilton result for braided monoidal 2-categories
summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber report obtaining an “Ekmann-Hilton” result for braided monoidal 2-categories as an application of their higher-operad framework.

sources.title: Algebras of higher operads as enriched categories II

label: Tensor product construction for A-infinity algebras
summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber state that their paper gives a construction of a tensor product of A-infinity algebras.
